subject: Urgent: Mercury Labs throughput spike — exec coordination & customer status
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@mercurylabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Mercury Labs Ops <ops@mercurylabs.com>; Samir Patel <samir.patel@mercurylabs.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — urgent

Irene,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and a burst of 5xx errors around 06:30 PT. Traffic pattern looks normal on our side; volumes are within expected. The front-end team is getting timeouts and our SLA SLO alerts are tripping.

What we need immediately:
- A short triage and a timeline for next steps (can you stand up a bridge?)
- Whether there will be any mitigation (fallback to smaller model or throttling) we can implement on our side

I know this is short notice — looping Samir (platform) and ops.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Reynolds

1) Observability: Karthik is pulling full request traces and model-level token latencies.
2) Mitigation: Ben will test a short-term routing rule to divert requests to the smaller quantized variant for the next 10 minutes.
3) CS comms: Marissa will prepare a short status note for your execs.
4) Escalation: David will open an incident record and track credits/impact.

Join the bridge: https://redwood.app/ops/incidents/INC-20261005-17 (starting now).

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 07:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — urgent

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 07:21 Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ava — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're booting an incident bridge now.

Quick status from instrumentation:
- Errors: 5xx rate rose from 0.02% to 1.8% at 06:28 PT, concentrated on the /v1/chat/generate route.
- Latency: p95 for token generation jumped from 420ms to 1.9s.
- Root cause signal: GPU queue latency on node pool gpul-eks-7 increased concurrently. Kernel-level backpressure looks consistent with a hotshard.

Planned short-term mitigations:
- Enable request shaping to limit concurrency per-client for Mercury for 15m. (Ben to push)
- Fall back to model rdx-7b-q4 (compatible) for Mercury routes — should reduce per-token tail latency.

I'll keep detailed traces on the bridge. I also attached a CSV with key metrics.

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mercury_metrics_1005.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 07:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — urgent

Pushed concurrency cap for Mercury Labs user token (cap=20) at 07:40 PT.
Fallback routing to rdx-7b-q4 enabled at 07:42 PT for their region-us routes. Metrics dropping already — p95 down to ~780ms and 5xx to 0.6%.

Notes:
- Throttle appears to reduce queueing but doesn't eliminate intermittent kernel stalls; working with infra to repro.
- No customer-visible data loss.

Ben Carter
On-call Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@mercurylabs.com>, ops@mercurylabs.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, david_kim@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency & 5xx spike — urgent

Ava / Mercury Ops — short update for your execs and customer-facing channel:

Status (08:05 PT):
- Impact: Increased p95 latency and transient 5xx spikes on /v1/chat/generate between 06:28–07:40 PT.
- Current: p95 ~760–820ms, 5xx ~0.4–0.7%. Traffic is being served via rdx-7b-q4 fallback; we applied a temporary per-customer concurrency cap.
- Customer action: No change required on your side. If you prefer, we can switch your app to retry/backoff for 502/503 during the next 10 minutes.

Action items and timeline:
- 08:15 PT: Karthik & infra to run kernel-level repro and log capture (target 30m investigation).
- 08:45 PT: Decision checkpoint — leave fallback in place vs. roll forward a hotfix.
- 09:30 PT: Post-mortem draft and MAP doc shared.

Attaching a draft mutual action plan and the metrics CSV. We'll keep the bridge open and will move to an exec summary at 10:00 PT for your leadership.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual_action_plan-draft.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@mercurylabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident update and executive summary — Mercury Labs (INC-20261005-17)

Ava — closing the loop after today's bridge. Short executive summary for Mercury leadership and our internal execs: 

Timeline and impact:
- 06:28 PT: p95 latency and 5xx spike observed (root cause: transient hotshard and GPU queue saturation on gpul-eks-7).
- 07:42 PT: Temporary fallback to rdx-7b-q4 + per-customer concurrency cap applied; customer traffic returned to nominal tail latency (~800ms p95).
- 07:50–17:30 PT: Stabilization window while infra ran repro; intermittent microbursts persisted but at <0.5% 5xx.

Customer commitments made:
- We will keep the fallback routing in place for the next 24 hours while we deploy a kernel patch and expanded capacity.
- A post-incident RCA + timeline for the kernel-level fix will be delivered by EOD tomorrow.
- We offered Mercury Labs 10% service credit for the impacted window; Marissa will coordinate contract language with finance if they accept.

Internal next steps:
- Karthik to open a follow-up engineering ticket for kernel backpressure root cause (ENG-14132).
- Ben to provision an expanded spare node pool for gpul-eks-7 and run soak testing.
- David to prepare the formal incident report and credit worksheet.

Docs & links:
- Incident: https://redwood.app/ops/incidents/INC-20261005-17
- MAP draft: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Mercury-MAP-2026-10-05
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-ML-8742

If Mercury execs would like an on-call briefing, I'm available 09:00–11:00 PT tomorrow.

Apologies again for the disruption, and thank you for the quick coordination — our priority is preventing recurrence and keeping your product SLAs intact.

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
